newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts close up after early boost from PPI data.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts close up after early boost from PPI data.

text.p: UK gilts closed up but off their highs on Monday after an early rally on strong Bunds and weak UK producer price data lost momentum later in the day.

The March gilt future settled 18/32 up at 109-17, off its intra-day high of 109-21. "The producer price data this morning was a further building brick...which decreased the chances of a rate rise," said one trader.

UK output prices rose a weaker-than-expected 0.5 percent in December giving a 1.7 percent annual rate, down from 2.1 percent in November. Seasonally adjusted input prices fell 0.5 percent in the month, giving a -5.9 percent year-on-year rate.

Coupled with anecdotal evidence last week of moderate pre-Christmas retail sales and weak data on manufacturing output, the PPI data reduces the chances of a rise in interest rates at Wednesday's monetary policy meeting, analysts said.

"If the Chancellor wants to keep interest rates steady at Wednesday's monetary meeting, this morning's PPIs give him useful ammunition with which to argue his case," said Bank America economist Jeremy Hawkins.
Analysts said the gilt curve had some scope to steepen should Chancellor Kenneth Clarke leave interest rates unchanged after his meeting with Bank of Enlgand governor Eddie George.

"Clarke will be very reluctant to raise rates, and in that instance we will continue to see the gilt curve steepen," said BZW gilts analyst Kevin Adams. "The short end will rally, leaving the long end vulnerable to a setback."
But one trader said the short end had risen so much recently, there was little room for further curve steepening.
"I don't know how much further it can go -- I'm not that bullish about the short end," he said.
The March short sterling contract settled two basis points higher on Monday at 93.47, implying official interest rates of around 6.50 percent at the end of the first quarter.
Gilts underperformed their German counterparts slightly on Monday with the 10-year gilt/Bund spread at 190 basis points in late trade versus 187 at the open.
